title: Write Equations
contentObjective: I can write an equation to represent a real-world situation.
languageObjective: I can explain my equation using the words equation, variable, equal sign, and expression.

noticeAndWonder.context: Detective Ruiz pins a clue to the board: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.' How could she rewrite this clue as an equation to crack the case?
noticeStarters: I notice the unknown number of gems can be called ___.
I notice 'plus 8 more' tells me to ___ 8.
I notice 'equals 20 total' tells me where the equal sign goes, so the equation is ___.
wonderStarters: I wonder how to write the whole clue as one equation.
I wonder how many gems were stolen.
I wonder how the equation changes if the clue said '8 fewer' instead.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Witness Count
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Ruiz interviews some witnesses on Monday, then 6 more on Tuesday, for a total of 21 witnesses. Write an equation using a variable to represent this situation.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Let w be the number of witnesses interviewed on Monday. The equation is w + 6 = 21.

turnAndTalk.question: Detective Ruiz's clue says 'a number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.' How would you turn this clue into an equation, and what does each part stand for?
turnAndTalk.kernel: I let a variable stand for the unknown number of gems.

stems.en: The unknown is ___, so I write the variable ___.
stems.es: La incógnita es ___, así que escribo la variable ___.

stems.en: My equation is ___ because 'plus 8' means ___ and 'equals 20' means ___.
stems.es: Mi ecuación es ___ porque 'más 8' significa ___ y 'es igual a 20' significa ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students choose a variable (such as n) for the unknown gems, build n + 8 = 20, and connect 'plus 8 more' to + 8 and 'equals 20 total' to = 20.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why does the equation n + 8 = 20 represent the clue better than the expression n + 8 alone? Justify using the role of the equal sign.
extendStems: The equation is better than the expression because ___.
The equal sign tells me ___ that an expression cannot show.

turnAndTalk.question: On the balance scale you put n + 8 on one side and 20 on the other. How did you decide what belongs on each side of the equal sign?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Both sides of the equation must represent the same total.

stems.en: I put ___ on the left side because ___.
stems.es: Puse ___ en el lado izquierdo porque ___.

stems.en: The equal sign means both sides are ___.
stems.es: El signo igual significa que ambos lados son ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students place the expression n + 8 on one side and the total 20 on the other, explaining the equal sign means both sides have the same value.
turnAndTalk.extend: Compare 'twice a number equals 20' with 'a number plus 8 equals 20.' How would the equations differ, and why?
extendStems: 'Twice a number' would be ___ instead of ___ because ___.
The operation changes the equation because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When would writing an equation help you solve a real problem instead of just guessing?
turnAndTalk.kernel: An equation organizes what I know and what I want to find.

stems.en: Writing an equation helps me because ___.
stems.es: Escribir una ecuación me ayuda porque ___.

stems.en: I would write an equation to find ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students explain that an equation captures the relationship clearly, lets you use a variable for the unknown, and can be solved instead of guessing.
turnAndTalk.extend: Critique: 'Any sentence with numbers is an equation.' Use the words expression and equal sign to explain why this is wrong.
extendStems: This is wrong because an expression ___.
A sentence is only an equation when it has ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Write Equations, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign.

stems.en: I put ___ on the left side because ___.
stems.es: Puse ___ en el lado izquierdo porque ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.8 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

mission.title: The Equation Vault
mission.story: You are Detective Ruiz's new code analyst. A tip just came in: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.' The evidence vault only opens when the clue is translated into a correct equation. Master writing equations and the case cracks wide open.
mission.objective: Translate word clues into equations with a variable so you can solve every case.

scenes.name: The Tip
scenes.text: Read the gem-theft clue and decide what the unknown quantity is.

scenes.name: Case Notes
scenes.text: Log the key terms: equation, variable, equal sign, and expression.

scenes.name: Evidence Balance
scenes.text: Use the balance scale to translate the clue into n + 8 = 20 and find n.

scenes.name: Clue Analysis
scenes.text: Translate the case clues. The lab adapts the difficulty to keep you sharp.

scenes.name: Stolen Art
scenes.text: Write an equation to track recovered paintings in a real heist.

scenes.name: Case Closed
scenes.text: File your report and prove you can turn any clue into an equation.

simulation.instructions: Translate the clue 'a number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total' into an equation, then balance the scale to find the unknown.
hints: The unknown is the number of stolen gems — call it n. The left side is n + 8; the right side is the total, 20.
Balance n + 8 = 20. Since 12 + 8 = 20, the scale balances when n = 12.

finale.title: Case Closed!
finale.text: Every clue translated, the vault sprang open, and the gems were recovered. Detective Ruiz just made you lead analyst — because you can turn any clue into an equation.

launch.narrative: Detective Ruiz received a tip: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total gems.' She needs to write an equation to represent this clue before she can solve the case. How would you write this situation as an equation?

conceptIntro.heading: How do I turn a word clue into an equation?
conceptIntro.intro: An equation is a math sentence with an equal sign (=). To write one, I pick a letter (a variable) for the unknown number and match the words to math symbols.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Clue: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.'
The unknown is the number of gems. I let n stand for it.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: New clue: 'A number plus 5 equals 9.' What is the unknown?
We let n be the unknown. What does 'plus 5' tell us to write?
What does 'equals 9' tell us? Put it together: n + 5 = 9.

lines: On the balance scale, build n + 8 = 20 and find what goes on each side.
Then write equations for the practice clues on your own.

explore.instructions: Use the balance scale to see how each word problem translates into an equation. Drag the correct expression to each side of the scale to make it balance.
hints: Read the situation: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.' The unknown is the number of stolen gems — that's n.
The left side is n + 8 (gems plus 8 more). The right side is 20 (the total). Balance them: n + 8 = 20.
explore.label: Build the equation on the balance scale. What goes on each side?

discourse.prompt: How did you decide what expression to put on each side of the balance?
discourse.sentenceFrame: I put ___ on the left side because ___, and ___ on the right side because ___. The equal sign means ___.

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'A number plus 12 equals 30'?
approaching.explanation: 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = 30.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
hints: Find the operation word in the sentence. What does 'plus' tell you to do with the number and 12?
Let n stand for the unknown number, then translate each phrase into symbols: 'a number' becomes n, 'plus 12' names an operation, 'equals 30' becomes = 30.
Build it left to right: n, then the symbol for 'plus', then 12, then '= 30'. Which choice matches that exact order?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Un número más 12 es igual a 30'?
hintsEs: Halla la palabra de operación en la oración. ¿Qué te dice 'más' que hagas con el número y el 12?
Deja que n represente el número desconocido y luego traduce cada frase a símbolos: 'un número' se vuelve n, 'más 12' nombra una operación y 'es igual a 30' se vuelve = 30.
Ármalo de izquierda a derecha: n, luego el símbolo de 'más', luego 12, luego '= 30'. ¿Qué opción coincide con ese orden exacto?

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'Seven less than a number is 18'?
approaching.explanation: 'Seven less than a number' means start with the number and subtract 7: n − 7 = 18.
choiceFeedback: Start with the variable, then subtract — not the other way.
The clue says "fewer" or "less" — use subtraction, not addition.
Use subtraction for "fewer" or "less," not division.
hints: 'Seven less than a number' is tricky — the number comes FIRST, and then 7 is taken away from it.
'Less than' flips the wording: '7 less than n' means start at n and subtract 7, not start at 7 and subtract n.
Write the number first: n, then subtract 7, then set it equal to 18. Which choice is built in that order?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Siete menos que un número es 18'?
hintsEs: 'Siete menos que un número' es tramposo: el número va PRIMERO y luego se le quitan 7.
'Menos que' invierte el enunciado: '7 menos que n' significa empezar en n y restar 7, no empezar en 7 y restar n.
Escribe el número primero: n, luego resta 7 y luego iguálalo a 18. ¿Qué opción está armada en ese orden?

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'Three times a number equals 21'?
approaching.explanation: 'Three times' means multiply by 3, so the equation is 3n = 21.
choiceFeedback: "Times" means multiply, not add.
Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
"Times" means multiply, not divide.
hints: Circle the operation word: 'times'. What operation does 'times' always signal?
'Three times a number' means 3 multiplied by n, written 3n with no symbol between the 3 and the n.
Put 3n on the left and set it equal to 21. Which choice shows multiplication instead of adding or subtracting 3?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Tres veces un número es igual a 21'?
hintsEs: Encierra la palabra de operación: 'veces'. ¿Qué operación señala siempre 'veces'?
'Tres veces un número' significa 3 multiplicado por n, y se escribe 3n sin ningún símbolo entre el 3 y la n.
Pon 3n a la izquierda e iguálalo a 21. ¿Qué opción muestra multiplicación en vez de sumar o restar 3?

approaching.stem: Which equation represents: 'A number divided by 4 equals 8'?
choiceFeedback: "Divided" means division, not multiplication.
Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
Use division here, not addition.
hints: The phrase 'divided by 4' names the operation. Which symbol shows division?
Keep the sentence order: the number n comes first, THEN it gets divided by 4.
Write n, then the division symbol, then 4 on the left side, and '= 8' on the right. Which choice matches exactly?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Un número dividido entre 4 es igual a 8'?
hintsEs: La frase 'dividido entre 4' nombra la operación. ¿Qué símbolo muestra división?
Conserva el orden de la oración: el número n va primero y DESPUÉS se divide entre 4.
Escribe n, luego el símbolo de división y luego 4 del lado izquierdo, y '= 8' a la derecha. ¿Qué opción coincide exactamente?

approaching.instructions: Sort each word phrase into the operation it represents.
hints: Read each phrase and think: does it mean combining, taking away, making groups, or sharing equally?
'More than' and 'sum' both mean addition. 'Less than' and 'fewer' both mean subtraction.
approaching.label: Sort each phrase into the correct operation.
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica cada frase en la operación correcta.
hintsEs: Lee cada frase y piensa: ¿significa combinar, quitar, formar grupos o repartir en partes iguales?
'Más que' y 'suma' significan ambas adición. 'Menos que' y 'menos' significan ambas sustracción.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: 'Plus 9' means add 9, not subtract. The correct equation is n + 9 = 15.
hints: Does 'plus' tell you to add or to subtract?
'A number plus 9' means n + 9, so the equation is n + 9 = 15.

onLevel.label: Match each situation to its equation

pairs.situation: A detective has some cases. After getting 9 new cases, she has 22.
A suspect's age divided by 3 equals 12.
Four times the number of fingerprints equals 28.
A detective had some clues. After removing 6, she had 15 left.

onLevel.hint: Read each item carefully, then match based on what the problem is asking.
hints: Underline the action in each situation: 'getting 9 new', 'divided by 3', 'four times', 'removing 6'. Each one names a single operation.
Match operations first: getting more means +, removing means −, 'times' means ×, 'divided' means /. Then check that the numbers agree too.
Try the first one: she has some cases (n) and GETS 9 more to reach 22 total. That is n plus something equals 22 — find the equation shaped that way.

rows.situation: A box holds some files. After removing 5, there are 13 left.
rows.variable: Number of files in the box

rows.situation: A detective split 48 photos equally into folders. Each folder has 6 photos.

onLevel.label: For each situation, identify what the variable represents and write the equation.
onLevel.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Row 1: the box starts with an unknown number of files — that unknown starting amount is exactly what n stands for.
Ask two questions for each row: What number don't we know? (that's n) What happened to it? (5 removed, or 48 photos split equally).
Row 1: removing 5 files is subtraction, and 13 remain — so write n, minus 5, equals 13. Then set up row 2 the same careful way.
onLevel.labelEs: Para cada situación, identifica qué representa la variable y escribe la ecuación.
hintsEs: Fila 1: la caja empieza con un número desconocido de archivos; esa cantidad inicial desconocida es exactamente lo que representa n.
Hazte dos preguntas en cada fila: ¿qué número no conocemos? (ese es n) ¿Qué le pasó? (se quitaron 5, o se repartieron 48 fotos en partes iguales).
Fila 1: quitar 5 archivos es resta y quedan 13, así que escribe n, menos 5, igual a 13. Luego arma la fila 2 con el mismo cuidado.

onLevel.stem: A detective found some fingerprints on Monday and 14 more on Tuesday, for a total of 30. Which equation represents this?
onLevel.explanation: The detective's Monday fingerprints (f) plus 14 more equals 30: f + 14 = 30.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: Monday's fingerprints are the unknown f. On Tuesday she found 14 MORE, and the two days together total 30.
'More' means the two amounts combine into one total. Combining to reach a total is addition, not multiplying or dividing.
Write it in story order: f (Monday) plus 14 (Tuesday) equals 30 (total). Which choice shows that sum?
onLevel.stemEs: Un detective encontró algunas huellas el lunes y 14 más el martes, para un total de 30. ¿Cuál ecuación representa esto?
hintsEs: Las huellas del lunes son la incógnita f. El martes encontró 14 MÁS, y los dos días juntos suman 30.
'Más' significa que las dos cantidades se combinan en un total. Combinar para llegar a un total es suma, no multiplicación ni división.
Escríbelo en el orden de la historia: f (lunes) más 14 (martes) es igual a 30 (total). ¿Qué opción muestra esa suma?

onLevel.label: Build the equation 2n + 3 = 11 on the balance scale and find n.
hints: The left side is 2n + 3. The right side is 11. What value of n makes both sides equal?
Try n = 4: 2(4) + 3 = 8 + 3 = 11. It balances!

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: Five times the number of suspects equals 35

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let s be the number of suspects

onLevel.correctWork: 'Five times the number' means multiply by 5, not add 5. The correct equation is 5s = 35.
hints: Does 'times' mean adding or multiplying?
'Five times the number of suspects' means 5 × s, so the equation is 5s = 35.

extending.title: Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: 'Twice' means multiply by 2, not add 2. The correct equation is 2n = 16.
hints: What does 'twice' really mean — adding or multiplying?
'Twice a number' means 2 times the number, so the equation is 2n = 16.

extending.prompt: Write a real-world situation that can be modeled by the equation n / 5 = 9. Explain what n represents and verify your equation makes sense.
extending.sentenceFrame: Situation: ___. In this problem, n represents ___. Check: n = ___ because ___ ÷ 5 = 9.
extending.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: n / 5 = 9 says: some amount n is split into 5 equal shares, and each share is 9. Think of things that get shared equally.
Pick a context — n stickers shared by 5 friends, n dollars split 5 ways. Say clearly what n counts, then check your value by multiplying 9 × 5.
Start your sentence: 'I had n ___ and split them equally among 5 ___; each got 9.' Then find n by computing 9 × 5 and checking it back.
extending.promptEs: Escribe una situación de la vida real que se pueda modelar con la ecuación n / 5 = 9. Explica qué representa n y comprueba que tu ecuación tiene sentido.
hintsEs: n / 5 = 9 dice: una cantidad n se reparte en 5 partes iguales y cada parte es 9. Piensa en cosas que se reparten por igual.
Escoge un contexto: n calcomanías repartidas entre 5 amigos, n dólares divididos en 5. Di claramente qué cuenta n y comprueba tu valor multiplicando 9 × 5.
Empieza tu oración: 'Tenía n ___ y los repartí en partes iguales entre 5 ___; a cada uno le tocaron 9.' Luego halla n calculando 9 × 5 y compruébalo.

rows.matches: Five identical bags hold 35 clues total.
rows.doesNotMatch: A detective has 5 more clues than 35.

rows.matches: After giving away 8 items, a detective has 12 left.
rows.doesNotMatch: A detective collected 8 items and then 12 more.

extending.label: For each equation, explain why one situation matches and the other does not.
extending.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Row 1: 5n = 35 means 5 EQUAL groups of n. Ask which situation really has equal groups and which one just adds more.
For each row, name the operation the equation uses (× or −), then test whether each situation's story truly uses that same operation.
Row 1: the non-match says '5 MORE clues' — 'more' signals addition, but 5n is multiplication. Explain that mismatch in your own words, then do row 2.
extending.labelEs: Para cada ecuación, explica por qué una situación corresponde y la otra no.
hintsEs: Fila 1: 5n = 35 significa 5 grupos IGUALES de n. Pregunta cuál situación de verdad tiene grupos iguales y cuál solo agrega más.
Para cada fila, nombra la operación que usa la ecuación (× o −) y luego prueba si la historia de cada situación realmente usa esa misma operación.
Fila 1: la que no coincide dice '5 pistas MÁS' — 'más' señala suma, pero 5n es multiplicación. Explica ese desajuste con tus palabras y luego haz la fila 2.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension: Crack the Mis-Written Clue

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: 5 less than the number of witnesses is 12

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let w be the number of witnesses

optional.correctWork: '5 less than w' means start with w and take away 5, so the equation is w − 5 = 12, not 5 − w = 12. The order matters: 'less than' flips the words but you still subtract from the number.
hints: Read 'less than' carefully — what number are you starting with before you subtract?
'5 less than w' is w − 5. The phrase '5 − w' would mean '5 minus the number,' which is a different clue.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Write Equations is reversing the order in 'less than' and 'fewer than' clues — writing 7 − n = 18 instead of n − 7 = 18 for 'seven less than a number is 18.' These phrases flip the words, but you still start with the unknown number and subtract from it. Before you submit, plug in your answer to check: for n − 7 = 18, n = 25 works because 25 − 7 = 18 ✓, but 7 − 25 = −18 ✗ shows the reversed equation is wrong.

watchFor.en: Listen for "Variable" — A letter that stands for a number that is unknown or can change.
watchFor.es: Escucha "Variable" — Una letra que representa un número desconocido o que puede cambiar.

watchFor.en: Listen for "Equal sign" — The = sign, showing both sides are the same.
watchFor.es: Escucha "Signo igual" — El signo =, que muestra que ambos lados son iguales.

tryTogether.scenarioEn: You are Detective Ruiz's new code analyst. A tip just came in: 'A number of stolen gems plus 8 more equals 20 total.' The evidence vault only opens when the clue is translated into a correct equation. Master writing equations and the case cracks wide open.
tryTogether.scenarioEs: Eres el nuevo analista de claves de la detective Ruiz. Acaba de llegar una pista: 'Un número de gemas robadas más 8 más es igual a 20 en total.' La bóveda de evidencia solo se abre cuando la pista se traduce en una ecuación correcta. Domina la escritura de ecuaciones y el caso se resolverá.

steps.en: Pick one practice problem and solve it on paper together.
steps.es: Elijan un problema de práctica y resuélvanlo en papel juntos.
steps.hintEs: Hablen de cada paso en voz alta.

steps.en: Check together: did you find the unknown, choose a variable, and turn the words into symbols around an equal sign?
steps.es: Verifiquen juntos: ¿hallaron la incógnita, eligieron una variable y convirtieron las palabras en símbolos alrededor de un signo igual?
steps.hint: This is the big idea of today's lesson.
steps.hintEs: Esta es la idea principal de la lección de hoy.

say.en: What part of the mission story helps here?
say.es: ¿Qué parte de la historia de la misión ayuda aquí?

say.en: Let's re-read the key idea together.

dontSay.en: This lesson is too hard — skip it.
dontSay.es: Esta lección es muy difícil — sáltenla.
